summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with a neutral shadow entity ('Room', from the Backrooms/Boys Vert style series) starting on b4. Room targets isolated pieces - pieces with NO neighbouring piece of either colour - and approaches one square per round; if the target is still alone when Room arrives, Room takes it. Room does not move when no isolated piece exists. Narrator keeps his pieces clustered, baits isolated enemy pawns and the queen, and wins.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
A piece is isolated if none of its 8 neighbouring squares holds any piece; enemy pieces DO count as neighbours.
Each round Room steps one king-step toward an isolated piece (nearest) of either colour; if the target is still isolated when Room reaches it, Room captures it.
If no isolated piece exists, Room does not move.
If the target gains a neighbour before Room arrives it is safe (Room retargets).
